editorial.description_en: Clay before it is fired, still holding water. Warmer and redder than the sand wall above it.
editorial.description_ja: 焼く前の粘土のような、やわらかい土の色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.806, C 0.048, h 62.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 粘 (nen, sticky) + 土 (do, earth) — the ordinary word for clay, used here as a colour name. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Raw Clay" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 粘土. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — suna-kabe at ΔE00 5.9, hi-kabe at ΔE00 6.1, kare-no at ΔE00 7.8. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (242°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
